channel.title: National Public Radio (NPR) - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from National Public Radio (NPR) (npr.org)

item.title: Dear Life Kit: I officiated their wedding. Now I think they should get a divorce
item.description: An NPR listener says they've become increasingly concerned by their friends' marriage and feels a sense of duty to fix their relationship problems. Can they tell them what they really think?

item.title: After a 2-decade ban, kites fill Lahore's skies during a Pakistani springtime festival
item.description: People gathered on rooftops to enjoy flying kites for the first time in years, celebrating the spring festival of Basant. The activity had been banned due to injuries and deaths during past celebrations.

item.title: What makes a good book-to-film adaptation? We have thoughts (and favorites)
item.description: Little Women (2019), Blade Runner (1982) and more favorites from NPR staff.

item.title: Meet the power couples of the 2026 Winter Games, from rivals to teammates
item.description: Some of these power couples span multiple sports, while others compete in the same discipline — or even on the same team.

item.title: It's a dangerous complication of pregnancy -- but a new drug holds promise
item.description: Researchers celebrate early results of a drug that may become the first treatment for a serious complication of pregnancy called preeclampsia. It's got the potential to save many lives.

item.title: 5 European nations say Alexei Navalny was poisoned and blame the Kremlin
item.description: In a joint statement, the foreign ministries of the U.K., France, Germany, Sweden and the Netherlands say Navalny was poisoned by Russia with a lethal toxin derived from the skin of poison dart frogs.

item.title: US military reports a series of airstrikes against Islamic State targets in Syria
item.description: The U.S. military says the strikes were carried out in retaliation of the December ambush that killed two U.S. soldiers and one American civilian interpreter.

item.title: American speedskater Jordan Stolz wins second Olympic gold with 500-meter race victory
item.description: With the win, Stolz joins Eric Heiden as the only skaters to take gold in both the 500 and 1,000 at the same Olympics.

item.title: Four people on NASA'S Crew-12 arrive at the International Space Station
item.description: The crew will spend the next eight months conducting experiments to prepare for human exploration beyond Earth's orbit.

item.title: Epstein files fallout takes down elite figures in Europe, while U.S. reckoning is muted
item.description: Unlike in Europe, officials in the U.S. with ties to Epstein have largely held their positions of power.
